subject: science
cluster: Stars, the Sun, and patterns in the sky
skillName: Patterns in Shadows, Day and Night, and Seasons

items.prompt:
A shadow is usually shortest
A) at sunrise
B) around noon
C) at sunset
D) at midnight

steps: The Sun is highest near noon, so shadows are shortest.

items.prompt:
Day and night repeat because
A) the Earth spins once each day
B) the Sun turns off
C) clouds move
D) the Moon blocks the Sun
items.answer: A) the Earth spins once each day

steps: Rotation turns each place toward and away from the Sun.

items.prompt:
Do the same stars appear every season?
A) Yes, always the same
B) No, different stars appear in different seasons
C) Stars never appear
D) Only in summer
items.answer: B) No, different stars appear in different seasons

steps: Visible constellations change with the seasons.

items.prompt:
A graph of shadow length from morning to evening looks like it
A) only goes up
B) starts long, is shortest near noon, then gets long again
C) stays flat
D) only goes down
items.answer: B) starts long, is shortest near noon, then gets long again

steps: Shadows shorten to a noon minimum, then lengthen.

items.prompt:
The seasonal pattern of constellations repeats about every
A) day
B) week
C) year
D) hour

steps: The same seasonal stars return each year.

items.prompt:
Graphing sky data instead of listing numbers is helpful because it
A) hides the pattern
B) makes the repeating pattern easy to see and predict
C) changes the data
D) is always wrong
items.answer: B) makes the repeating pattern easy to see and predict

steps: Graphs reveal trends that support predictions.

items.prompt:
It is daytime in one country and night in another at the same moment because
A) the Sun splits in two
B) Earth's rotation makes one side face the Sun while the other faces away
C) one country has no Sun
D) clouds block one country
items.answer: B) Earth's rotation makes one side face the Sun while the other faces away

steps: Only the side facing the Sun has daylight at a given moment.

items.prompt:
A daylight-hours graph is short in winter and long in summer and repeats each year. You can use it to
A) predict daylight for the same months next year
B) change the seasons
C) stop the Earth spinning
D) nothing
items.answer: A) predict daylight for the same months next year

steps: A repeating yearly pattern supports predictions for future years.
